About / Michal WochnaPROFILE

IT & BUSINESS SYSTEMS MANAGER

Hi, I’m
Michal Wochna_

I manage IT and business systems at Advanced Safety, a PPE and safety equipment supplier in Castlebar.

That covers the ERP, the warehouse management system, the CRM and the webshop, the vending and Kanban systems our customers use on site, and the infrastructure, Microsoft 365 and security underneath all of it.

A good part of this I design, build and maintain myself. The rest I configure, integrate and keep running, working closely with sales, customer service, the warehouse and production so that the systems fit the way people actually work.

Work / Advanced Safety

01

The systems,
and the people using them.

I have been at Advanced Safety for over fifteen years. In that time the role has grown from IT support into responsibility for the company’s business systems: ERP, WMS, CRM, eCommerce and the customer-facing vending, Kanban and garment-fitting services.

Much of what we run was designed and built in house. I own those systems end to end, from the first requirement through to the integrations, the reporting and the day-to-day maintenance.

01

ERP, WMS & data

Intact iQ ERP and the warehouse management system: implementation, configuration, reporting, and the data checks that keep stock, pricing and product information reliable across every system that depends on them.

02

eCommerce, CRM & integrations

The Aphix webshop, the Freshsales CRM and the integrations that connect them to the ERP. Product data, ordering workflows, automated email and the internal tools that join the systems up.

03

Vending, Kanban & fitting services

Managed PPE for customer sites: vending machines, Kanban replenishment and the garment-fitting service. I designed the software behind these, including the dashboards, usage reporting and replenishment logic, and I maintain it.

04

Infrastructure, security & support

Microsoft 365, Teams, SharePoint, network, servers and backups, plus support for colleagues. My cybersecurity work shapes how access, configuration and risk are handled across the business.

I run development work in short, reviewable increments, and I map a process properly before automating it. The technology is only useful if it fits the job it is there to support.

Qualifications / Education & training

02

Experience,
backed by study.

I returned to education while working full time, completing a Higher Diploma in Computing, a Postgraduate Diploma in Cybersecurity and then an MSc, all with First Class Honours.

The study runs alongside the job rather than separately from it. The MSc dissertation grew out of email security questions I was already dealing with at work, and it became the basis for TrustIndex and trustscan.

Backstory / Before the job title

03

It started with
a Commodore 16.

I was born in Poland in 1980. My dad brought home a Commodore 16 when I was small, and the two of us would go to the giełda komputerowa at the weekend to look for parts and cassettes. The C64 came next, then an Amiga 500, and I have never really stopped since.

Through the nineties it was PCs: 286, 486, Pentium. I built them, took them apart, chased memory settings and spent a lot of evenings in CONFIG.SYS and AUTOEXEC.BAT. I wanted to know what was going on inside the box, and that curiosity has not gone anywhere.

I also taught people to use computers, from switching one on for the first time through to Windows and the TAG word processor. Later I studied geography and trained as a teacher. Explaining a system clearly, and helping someone feel at ease with it, is still a large part of what I do.

C16 → C64 → AMIGA 500 → PC

Outside work

04

There’s usually
a computer involved.

At home I run a Proxmox homelab and look after my own network, and I like hands-on work: soldering, repairing old hardware and keeping a Commodore 64 running. I game on Xbox as well, usually something long like Cyberpunk or Fallout.

I came to running late and I am still new enough to enjoy every small improvement. I cycle and swim too.

Most of all, I have two boys. I gave them their first computers and games, the way my dad did for me, and I am proud to be passing that on.
